aggregate_brief: Today's standouts: GB Power — 98th-percentile of 5-yr range — historically high; Clean Spark — 94th-percentile of 5-yr range — historically high; Coal — 7th-percentile of 5-yr range — historically low.

news.geopolitics_summary: European heat waves and wildfire risk mounting; US gas production at record levels; Iran sanctions uncertainty; Rosatom safety concerns threaten EU nuclear strategy.

themes.headline: US natural gas production forecast to hit record 122.5 Bcf/d in 2026
themes.why_it_matters: Record US LNG export capacity will increase arbitrage pressure on TTF and front-month gas prices. Lower US production costs (Permian super-laterals noted separately) reinforce competitive LNG flows to NW Europe, capping winter Cal+1 and storage filling costs.

themes.headline: France faces budget crunch amid historic heat wave impacts
themes.why_it_matters: Budget constraints may delay French nuclear maintenance and renewable capex. Reduced capex headroom pressures French supply-side capacity, risking higher DA power spreads and EUA upside if coal/gas substitution occurs during outages.

themes.headline: Marine heat waves and ocean warming driving extreme European weather patterns
themes.why_it_matters: Ocean warming amplifies summer cooling demand and wildfire risk, raising peak-hour power demand and constraining hydro/wind ramps. Persistent heat also depresses thermal efficiency. Net upside to summer Cal+1 and Q3 power curves; EUA bullish if coal-backing rises.

themes.headline: Rosatom safety violations alleged; concerns raised on Hungary Paks II project
themes.why_it_matters: If Paks II (500+ MW) faces sanctions or regulatory delay, Hungary's baseload capacity tightens. EU would rely more on gas/coal for backup, raising power prices and EUA demand; sanctions risk on Russian nuclear fuel also threatens long-term EU supply strategy.

themes.headline: Permian operators boost output via longer horizontal wells (15,000+ ft super-laterals)
themes.why_it_matters: Marginal cost reduction in US gas production supports elevated LNG exports. Lower breakeven encourages more arbitrage-driven LNG cargoes to Europe, keeping TTF depressed relative to seasonal norms and weakening summer power spreads.

watchlist: French budget vote / nuclear maintenance schedule announcements — capacity risk over autumn/winter.
EU sanctions decision on Rosatom and Paks II timeline — impacts Hungarian baseload and EU ETS substitution demand.
European wildfire season peak (Aug–Sep) — transmission outages and hydro availability volatility.
US LNG export-capacity bottleneck relief or further delays — direct TTF arbitrage driver.
